reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that emotions are not abstract entities but structured combinations of physiological and cognitive components. The decomposition primitive formalizes this by treating emotional states as sums over sensory-motor elements: E = Σ F_i. Each F_i represents a distinct physiological correlate such as heart rate or facial muscle tension. When these are removed, the residual emotional state R = E - Σ F_i becomes undefined or trivial. This leads to a dual structure: one where emotional states are fully specified by their correlates (physiological), and another where they are reduced to mere cognition (affective residualism). The independence primitive asserts that each physiological element is essential—removing one breaks the integrity of the emotional construct. Thus, the failure mode occurs when either the physiological basis is absent or the cognitive framework fails to integrate the sensory data. These primitives form a closed system under which GSI can model emotional inference and GSE can simulate emotional dynamics.
